verdict.tagline: A striking isometric action game hindered by technical friction.
for_you_if: you want an intense action challenge
you plan to play past the early campaign
not_for_you_if: you need stable frame rates during boss fights
you get motion sickness from intense visual effects
you require keyboard and mouse controls

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the character creation system produces unattractive or misshapen character models.

citations.review_text:
Change this when they fix character creator.

The character creator is atrocious, even for a start, you're literally picking between potatoes looking people, the cinematic characters look great but when you make one they look damn dreadful, give us some better options and give us some attractive options.

Maybe there is a good game under there but these dirty and muddy visuals kill it for me. Looking too long at the screen gives you eye strain. The messy art style, dim lighting and overuse of particles everywhere makes the game lose all visual clarity. I only played about on hour before I refunded it, so I don't know if this gets better as the game progresses.
In addition the character's body proportions look broken, making it impossible to create a somewhat decent character. My hero looks like a birth defect with monkey arms.
Art is subjective however, so If you don't mind the questionable art style you might have fun with this one. I think the underlying game might be quite solid.

citations.review_text:
Game intro sucks.  Game requires a gamepad, key/mouse controls do not work.

Big nope on this crap.  Sadly too busy with real life, ran out of time to refund.

Its a no for me. I'd give it 3 stars cus I'm sure it will appeal to some people.

But for me its a no.  The camera "controls" (or lack there of) are bad.  You miss stuff cus you cant get perspective.  Loot is a pain - everything looks the same.  Jump puzzles and agility puzzles 100% do not belong in a game with this style of controls and camera.   That was probably the worst.  The combat is OK - Just the right difficulty but I hate non-responsive combats.  I like a faster paced combat - I really don't enjoy staring at an enemy waiting to punish their actions.  Snooze.  But that's just preference.

My friends and I played a few hours and decided we had better games to enjoy.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience severe frame rate drops and stuttering during daytime lighting conditions or in cities, even on high-end hardware.

citations.review_text:
The game looks amazing, the controls are crisp, you can explore to your hearts content. I spent 90% of my current my playtime in the first area of the game, looking through every nook and cranny.

The lore and worldbuilding? Immaculate

The voices, the characters and the cutscenes? A joy to hear and watch.

The performance? At night, great. During the day when the sun is up and the game has to calculate lighting? Abysmal, why does this game even require a recommended 32Gb of ram? I have a really strong PC but during daytime this game turns into a slowmotion cinematic.

I would recommend the game, it is amazing, but with the current performance even people with 5090s are having issues and that's not okay. So it is a no from me, until we get an optimization update from the devs. Maybe with 1.0

This game is actually incredible. I don't really care for these types of games, this is an exception its like helldivers or something came out of no where and is just 10/10 gameplay, it rewards exploration, the story seems really genuine and cool the opposite of modern gamer slop, the combat is limited only by the weapons, not some archaic system, lots of cool weapons styles to chose from, like a  scyth?! its just sick. lots of in world interactions ( I pet every cat) 

1 MAJOR con. this game fricken lags unbelievably. I left my pc stats so you can see. you will absolutely need a frame generation tool for this. with a 3090 ti overclocked no matter what I do, I can get 10 fps in cities. like your settings have nothing to do with performance. hosted servers from devs issue? if it was in world I would give it a 4 out of 10. which would hurt my soul to do because this game is my new home for awhile. thats literally the only can I can think of so far and my god is it a bad one. sigh.

(UPDATE) So I moved my game to the fastest ssd I had 7800mb write and 6800 read. that made a big difference.

Rather frustrating to play...
- sprint does auto jump, rather than letting me jump on my own.
- jumping ends up lacking precision where it lands, which makes you miss and fall.
- Interaction prompts are flimsy as hell... you need to be on the exact spot for the prompt to show up, be it fishing or other interactions. So often i find myseld trying to do small tweaks to the position of my character just trying to figure out the prompt to show up.
- Status warns me when my friend levels up, which is not useful, but does not warn me of the loot being picked by my friend, which would be useful (since once they pickup you have nothing left to pickup).
- in FHD resolution, with a RTX 4090, it tanks the FPS in certain areas to bellow 40, 30, even bellow 20 in some extreme cases.
- For display there is nice options, but for graphics you only have overall quality settings not able to specifically tune shadow, etc quality.
- Trying to revive the other player, with enemies around/targeting me, decides to cut the 2 trees or pickup mushrooms rather than reviving my friend...
- Sometimes fails to grab to stairs/vines and walks over them... making you fall instead (with deadly consequences sometimes). In some vines I had to try 5 times before it would actually grab them because it would just walk over the edge..
- When using gamepad, configuring the runes shortscuts (which are 2 key combinations), it conflicts with the parry key (single key input), even though it should not. (Only happens with parry and not the other action buttons).

I understand this is a early access and it is clearly so, even though it is now 2 years old "early access".
Thus I am not refunding and i am in hopes these things get fixed by next year.

TLDR:
- The game is pretty, the world seems interesting, the voice acting is cool also.
- But the gameplay issues, multiplayer QoL and lack of FPS optimization are taking the fun away.
- Lets wait a year and see.

If relevant, I was playing with keyboard and mouse.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe platforming and jumping mechanics as difficult to control, leading to accidental falls.

citations.review_text:
I guess i would overall recommend this game.
But it has a whole bunch of issues that are too much of a hassle to enjoy the good part.

* Getting materials is way too much of a chore. Even if you like farming stuff its incredibly tedious. Every time you cut down a tree or mine, there is a quicktime event. Then 2 items fall off that you then have to manually pick up. And character is so sensitive so you have to be facing the material you're picking up. And you need a ton of materials for every upgrade and craft. It's awful.

* There are no indications on which plants are materials or just background. Same with most resources and chests. If you have even slightly bad eyesight you will miss them.

* As resources are so scarce, after each battle you will find yourself looking for stuff rather than continuing your adventure.

* Jumping between platforms is hard to align. The isometric view together with several floors and decoration makes it hard to judge where you are going to land. So falling to your death will be common.

* In order to respec your failed character build, you have to progress in a crucible. Which is for obvious reasons a dumb mechanic.

* A bit too often the game says: "Sould-like for thee, Diablo style for me". They aimed at not designing the game as an "Aoe until its all dead". But thats often precisely what you get from both player and mobs.

It's fun. There needs to be some more balancing though. Also, movement needs tweaks because the clambering mechanic and auto-jump has made me fall by mistake too many times. Sprint an clamber are one using the same button. You also need to sprint to auto-jump. Sometimes you will clamber over a small rock when trying to jump and then your character proceeds to jump from a cliff. For a game that seems to focused on vertical exploration, we should have more control with jumping and climbing. As for exploration, it is fun...but the full game better have more direction. EA has very little directive side quests from what I can tell. You have a large side quest and then the main quest and they both progress very nicely...and then it just stops. So odd. I question the rationale for daily and weekly challenges and real-time merchant stock. This game doesn't need it. It isn't a seasonal live service ARPG.

pc controls, especially WASD are extremely clunky, most of the time you are fighting poor controls and targeting in a world where you fall off every edge or get stuck on any terrain. dodging enemies (that have unlimited stamina and no cooldown on their movesets btw) and getting stuck on a tree and then getting stunlock by infinite attack spamms and die, feels horrible, this is not difficulty, its clunkiness. some people don't mind this, good for them. but this has nothing to do with "get good" if its no fun in the first place.

oh btw, no dedicated jump button in a game were terrain traversal is necessary, you taking the wrong auto jump angle, fall 5 floors to your death, with durability loss, and you have to climb your way up again just to fall of a ledge because the auto grip didn't work? yeah no.....

i was progressing steadily, I just got annoyed by constant game design choices, 
the game itself is not hard, moves are predictable, you got more then enough tools for the job. the whole stamina exhaustion and poise system punishes the clunky WASD movement even more, that sometimes you ask yourself, what could i have done to improve? nothing, you just got unlucky that a boss threw you into a tree, you got stunned, and then jeetet of a cliff because you couldnt control your dodge movement as precice as you wanted. for the X amount of time in a row. it just doesn't feel right. and no i will not go dust of my controller...

i will come back when the game is released. maybe try to tinker with the controlls more, MAYBE yes try controller (i really dislike games that only feel right on controller). but as of now, i wish i could refund this...

This game has the worst jumping mechanic of all the games i have played.
I would give it like 8.5/10 but with this it is like barely a 6.

Honestly, I want to like this game. Aesthetically, its great. Conceptually, it introduces a lot of fun little extra spins on the ARPG genre. Its got a lot of good stuff to it. But it also has a ton of just horrifically baked mechanics it has decided to lean on hard enough to make me call it a loss.
1) Idle game mechanics. I suspect they wanted to try to make it immersive, but without any kind of animation or visual indicators or logic, it just feels like those games who want you to pay money to speed up the process. Oh, you want to turn these logs into planks? Stick 8 of your 60 logs in here, and come back in 4 minutes so you can stick the next 8 in here. Just because you can't pay real money to speed it up doesn't make it absolute trash.
2) Inconsistent parry. This is a pretty simple rule for games. If you have parry, and you have moves that can't be parried, have VERY clear indicators to let me know, so I don't just have to try again and again to determine "nope, guess this move probably can't be parried. Glad I died 5 times to figure out this trash mob's can be parried list." I should know what is and isn't parried WITHOUT parrying a single blow.
3) Drunk movement. The parkour mechanic is honestly cool. But more often than its cool, its frustrating because your character jumps when he shouldn't, doesn't when he should, or whatever. And it is really, really boring to walk back somewhere because your character died falling off a ledge while drunk. If they tightened up the movement, it would be cool. Because its not, its terrible.
4) Dodge is just too good. I am trying to build a heavy armor build. I practiced it, I built towards it. Then, out of frustration, I just went nude in a zone 3 times my level. Instatnly went deathless and blitzed through it because the naked dodge is just way too good compared to the aforementioned inconsistent parry and fat roll. There is no good incentive besides making the game harder (a legit incentive, mind you) to wear armor.

Anyway…

Enemies can swith between ranged attacks and melee attacks so fast it feels like cheating, but most enemies can jump fully across the screen at lightnign speed to kill you. AOEs are very hard to read, it's hard to know if you'll be able to dodge out of the way of firebombs or giant sweeping attacks with laughably enormous swords. Your stamina runs out in twwo hits and then you just... stand there and die. There are loads of stunlock attacks where you just... stand there and die. It's easy to get swarmed and there are no tools to deal with it. I die a lot and I never really know what to do to improve because the game doesn't seem to want to tell me how to improve.

God I wanted to enjoy it, but it's a soulslike.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience frame rate drops and stuttering performance, particularly in the city and during specific areas.

citations.review_text: love it, cant wait for 1.0 , really hope they optimize some aspects like in the city that the frame rates drops awfuly bad, besides that 100% would recommend

This game is awesome! The story is interesting, and the animation is really smooth. It’s a very beautiful and intriguing world. I just want to keep coming back to this game over and over again. There are a couple of spots where the FPS starts to drop, but I think they’ll fix that over time. The main downside is that there’s no full-fledged endgame. The combat is really cool, and I’d love to play another 50 hours, but there’s nowhere to go. Just running around gets boring. The daily quests get tedious too—one reward per day… I hope there will be a good endgame in the future. Overall, everyone should definitely play through the game, if only for the story.

10 /10. Absolutely love this game. im a huge souls like fan, but this isnt a clone. this is its own beast. Art is 10 out of 10, beautiful game. Story 10/10 i want more!!!! more side quests more DLCs more characters. love it. Boss battles 10/10. Design level and enemy 10/10. im hesitant to say this but id rather get a larger no rest for the wicked for a no rest for the wicked 2, over a dark souls 4. im excited for the full release and iv been checking regularly for any word on updates or added quests. im apparently 80 hours in and im build tweaking in the end game. i havnt even came close to trying out 1/2 the builds yet.  

Now the Bad- story is short. if you have the right build and are not an explorer, and you dont max out all of the town upgrades i feel you can beat the story in 6-8 hours. 
Performance is odd. it will run beautifully then just's studder up, and limited control on grafics tweaking- pretty much you can control the render %. 
Some of the enemies' hit boxes are misleading and can be frustrating- but not even remotely a deal breaker.

Very excited for the full release. I was kind of dissapointed once I learned there will be a wipe at 1.0, so I decided to stop playing until the game leaves early access. I hope the developer does fix that before the full release, because preformance issues definitly pulls me out of the immersion.

I like the game. I like the exploration. I like fighting enemies and bosses. I like the art design and level design.

What kills the fun for me is the constant material grind and the constant inventory management. What makes this even worse is that tools have a durability and it takes too much time to get the resources.
The game just feels unnecessarily time consuming and punishing in areas where it shouldn't be. I need material X, go to area A, run around, kill and loot stuff, need to get back to the town, because my inventory is full, run to my chest, run to sell items, then go back to area A, run to where i left of... The gameplay and world are sooo nice and fun, but I am held back by the feeling that the game wants to waste my time with the wrong things. I also don't like the gem system and destroying one thing or the other... again it just feels unnecessary and like they want me to waste more time. I just want to have fun and be able to try things. There is no added value for me.

And don't get me wrong I play many games where you need to grind materials or XP and I like games with many systems that I need to feed with items and time, but here it feels too unrewarding and unfun and I just started the game.

claims.claim: Reviewers find that furniture placement controls during housing customization are cumbersome and difficult to position precisely.

citations.review_text:
So far a really fun game with awesome graphics, satisfying combat and great story. The voice acting is also really good! 

Only thing that still needs some work is the housing system. The idea is nice, but the way they did the placing of furniture is extremely painful. Why not let players select an item they want to place and be able to just move that object in the room/space, for example with your mouse or joystick, instead of having to move it around with your character. I play with M&K and it takes ages to get furniture placed "just right".

all around it's pretty fun. few issues though, latency problems in multiplayer, could use a way to two hand one handed weapons like dark souls/elden ring, and if you're running bows or magic there should be a way to cancel a spell or cancel a drawn bow so you can dodge instead of getting smacked in the face, maybe also make the community chest bigger or have unlimited slots because it runs out of space fast even if you only use it for resources because it forces you to grind money and the resources to buy a house and make chests. thats kind of rough for people that like exploring, looting and questing over city building. those are the only things noticed so far

claims.claim: Reviewers state that resource gathering and town upgrading require extensive grinding and backtracking through previously cleared areas.

citations.review_text:
I’m a bit hesitant about making this a positive review, but the core of this game is quite good. I’ve enjoyed the combat, story, and progression so far very much.

However I have one fairly large issue and two smaller gripes that have been impeding my enjoyment. The resource gathering required for just about everything is too much in my opinion and the backtracking that would be required to get everything you need legitimately would be egregious. There’s currently 3 tiers of the basic materials in the game (wood and minerals) and when you move into a higher level area with the next tier of materials to gather the lower tier mats you’d need to run through the areas you’ve previously spent a good chunk of time in just chopping down trees and mining. When I got to the area with the second tier of mats and saw that to upgrade my shops I would need to go reclear the first areas until I had chopped down well over 100 trees and mine like 50 copper nodes… I think the gear crafting and upgrade costs are tuned about right, but most other things could have their costs cut by 50-75% and in my eyes this would go from a glaring problem to being at worst a mild annoyance but probably would be fine. Alternatively any way to passively generate a portion of the resources or a way to break higher tiered resources into large batches of low tier ones would also help a lot. I don’t really consider pressing triangle on ore veins and trees to be good gameplay when compared to the rest of what the game offers, but it would have bothered me a lot less if it didn’t also require running through low level areas solely to press triangle on low level trees. A similar issue for me is that the whispers in the this game (think bonfires in Souls) have to have gear/resources/currency sacrificed to them before you can fast travel to them. The high costs for fast travel and shop upgrades have definitely impacted my enjoyment.

My first minor gripe is an annoyance with certain enemy movesets. I typically…

If you just want to follow the story you're are constantly under leveled. You have to do the grind-loot-grind loop to make progress. Most of the gear is useless and upgrading becomes more and more of a chore looking for materials. As the world is not procedural generated - which is a huge plus for me - this kind of gameplay however becomes repetitive very quickly, visiting the same places over and over without anything new. I think the game would be better without all the grinding, looting and crafting.

And the game is still full of bugs: Stuck walking animation, invisible enemies...

the concept is incredibly fun, the gameplay was terrific until i've hit the grind point for resources.
It just doesen't feel that rewarding, nor fun, to go back into previously explored location and start looking for trees, cut them, same with ore, same with fish, same with digging. There just isn't a world where I'm cutting trees for an hour to roll for a better bow enchant. The chests are in a similar spot. I really hate going around the map ive previously explored, opening the same chests I've opened for a chance of a research paper. I think adding some way of grinding resources (like wood, ore, etc) and some more reliable source of research papers or upgrade mats would be a good idea.

I like the game. I like the exploration. I like fighting enemies and bosses. I like the art design and level design.

What kills the fun for me is the constant material grind and the constant inventory management. What makes this even worse is that tools have a durability and it takes too much time to get the resources.
The game just feels unnecessarily time consuming and punishing in areas where it shouldn't be. I need material X, go to area A, run around, kill and loot stuff, need to get back to the town, because my inventory is full, run to my chest, run to sell items, then go back to area A, run to where i left of... The gameplay and world are sooo nice and fun, but I am held back by the feeling that the game wants to waste my time with the wrong things. I also don't like the gem system and destroying one thing or the other... again it just feels unnecessary and like they want me to waste more time. I just want to have fun and be able to try things. There is no added value for me.

Flipped a coin and landed on "yes", hence it's thumbs up from me.
The review is from early access, supposedly the next update is going to bring the full release of the game, along with job/class system and weapon rebalance. We'll see how it goes.

ANYWAY, welcome to my quick review of Identity Crisis: The Game. 

Why 'Identity Crisis' I hear you ask? Because this game is trying to be everything at once. You have isometric view somewhat similar to Path of Exile, Diablo, or Last Epoch, and systems like affixes/mods and gems for your items - kind of in between what you see in the games I just mentioned. However, you also have Elden Ring style combat (far more forgiving tho, and actually playable on the keyboard), gear durability FOR WHATEVER REASON, daily and weekly quests - even in singleplayer! - like it's some kind of MMORPG, absurd amounts of resource gathering like it's some kind of Stardew Valley, and town building system where you have to farm and refine said resources in order to donate them to the city and restore/upgrade establishments of various NPCs. Uou can also own a house (or a whole bunch of them) and use furniture to decorate each one of them to your liking. We're only missing crops management and tower/city defense mechanics... oh, right, don't forget to cook your meals so you can heal properly!

Don't get me wrong, No Rest For The Wicked does *most* of this stuff well enough to not be a pain in the rear end. Even cutting down 60 trees for a weekly isn't as bad as it may sound at first, but it's not a 10 minute ordeal either. It's just *wicked* to me how many different mechanics has been shoved into this one game simply because they can be added and not because they are needed. It may work for some, might not work for the others; I'm fine with most of the things I just mentioned as I like diversity, but I think that daily and weekly quest system in a game like that is simply ridiculous and trying to keep up with them for a while made me not wan…

claims.claim: Reviewers note that upgrade materials can be hard to farm and request a deconstruct table to recover materials from unwanted gear.

citations.review_text: This one is stunning. It feels like you're a part of a fantastic story projected on an oil painting. Every area a delight. But a dangerous one. Any misstep can lead to your (inevitable) demise. Alas, the risk is worth it, as a myriad of secrets are just beyond the obvious path. NRftW blends perfectly the Action part of an ARPG with the intense Danger of enemies and environment. On top of that you have an abundance of mechanics to explore and master. Although not fully released yet, the game feels already way better than a vast majority of triple-A titles that came up lately. Well worth to play - although I'd recommend buying it now (it's past mid-August at the time of this review) and wait for its October full release (they'll do a full wipe). Also, to provide some constructive criticism - as for some items the upgrade mats farm is really hard, I think we could really use a deconstruct table to have a chance to recover some mats from the gear we don't need. Thank you devs for all you've built here! I wish you all a long and prosperous life! :)

Gear lock feature: A lock option for weapons and armor to prevent accidentally dismantling or selling them.
​Reviewing the inventory storage size: Re-evaluating the player's inventory or stash capacity.
​Consumable animation speed: Faster animations when using healing items or potions.
​Gear salvaging system: Adding a feature to dismantle weapons or armor to reclaim their core components or raw materials.
​Yellow Amber enhancement adjustment: When using Yellow Amber on weapons or armor, we hope for a system that allows rerolling or changing negative enhancements.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that character movement can feel clunky, leading to accidental deaths from falling off ledges or cliffs.

citations.review_text:
Before we go any further: Even if they stopped working on the game now it is worth every cent and I have gotten my monies worth twice over. 
Art style is amazing
music is great
game is extremely fun just wish there was more currently
movement can be clunky and a headache at times causing you to take way longer to do easy tasks
the map and teleport points should be easier to figure out where you are traveling in the menus and when looking on the map
falling to your death because of the horrible movement of the character or due to a combo in crucible is dumb
there are a few waste time mechanics listed above and a couple more in game that take away from what seems to be a great game without the need for these known fixable time sinks

I have put in about 100 hours in the game, and I'm still gathering resources to make my build and have a comfy home.
Beat the game and the crucible on the hardest difficulty with a brother in arms, still gathering resources and upgrading my equipment. 
Love fishing and running around and opening chest. 
Died many times because I kept on falling from high areas.
10/10 would buy this game 10 times if I could.

It is a great game! Many different builds to try. Love the effort they put into creating the world and all the little hidden loot spots (gotta love the reward for looking at every nook of each area, even if it is just a regular material piece) etc. Love the feel of the game and design. It shows that they put a lot of effort and love in the game. The only thing I find quite annoying as a mouse/keyboard player is the diagonal boards or passages that lead to a jump and how you have to position and try to find the correct angle before a jump. Some are not easily reached by pressing a and d at the same time, it is not exactly a 45 degree jump, more like 35 let's say so it requires a looot of effort to get to them (at least for me :P ). Don't get me wrong, I do enjoy a challenge, but not on 85% of the places that are normally out of reach and require 'parkour' to get to them. If I remember correctly the game does mention that it is better to play with a controller, however I don't own one and have jumped off cliffs and various hights to my death many times  trying to reach a 'hidden place' due to this issue :P! Amazing game other than that small difficulty I face as a mouse/keyboard player and would deffo recommend it!!!

claims.claim: Reviewers experience random crashes, disconnects, loading errors, and performance spikes when multiple players use heavy elemental damage.

citations.review_text:
I'm enjoying the game for what it is - a classless ARPG where i can build characters the way i want. After nearly 180 hours, I have achieved what i set out to achieve twice - my characters being able to solo final bosses at the hardest difficulty. 

What I am most sad about: The save wipe then 1.0 comes about. I will miss my characters and realms. I really hope there is some way we can still play the "legacy early access" game while still playing the new one.

What i dont like: The game has random crashes, disconnects, loading errors and weird character actions. I hate the progress circle when fishing. It is tiny and should be on the fish and not on the character. I dont like that we cant cancel actions like fishing or mining mid way. there is no key for that so you are caught "pants down" if an enemy comes. I dont like that there is also no parry or block indicator and that all enemies are so different that it would take too long to learn for the casual dad player like me. I dont like bugs using radiant embers and the exaltation system. sometimes pants only upgrade to crit chance of 4 max. while it should be 5. sometimes exalting takes it to 5 then it cant go to 6 when you use your radiant ember. Just wasted the radiant ember which is EXTREMELY hard to find. I also dont like that the game has performance spikes especially when there are 4 people with heavy elemental damage. That lag can be the deciding factor between a loss and win. Items should also have a lock system but i think the devs are on to that already.

What i like: Classless character building. Beautiful worlds. Great story. Every weapon has a different animation, style, character and runes. SO awesome. A discord community which I can trade items with especially when items like radiant embers are so hard to come by. Fast loading between levels. Playing daily with my friends!

TLDR: I would build more characters with different weapons and armour sets if radiant and essence ember drops were not so…

It took me around 25 hours to get better at this game
Of course, the game is not just about difficulty; it's punishing too.

Not gonna lie, I want to thumb down and review against the game. But considering the upside of the game's presentation. I think I'm positive with the game.

Pros
- Overall visuals are stunning!
- Theme and setting go well together
- The combat is very unique, and it's not too difficult in the first hour of the game
- Can co-op
- Many selection of weapon choices
- Has a town upgrade system that is well-designed
- Many unique dialogue lines for NPCs
- SFX (as well as BGM) is neat!

Cons: (first of all, I used to dislike the game at first due to all of these personal opinions, and I know some of you guys who's the expert reading this will consider me a 'skill issue'. And I don't think that I'm the only one who felt this way; look up Reddit, the game's forum, and Steam discussions. Many threads say the same thing as I wrote these)
(My main playthrough is Two-Handed Melee weapon, co-op with my friend who's into ranged and mage)
- Melee and parry are sad :( The game is too punishing for close-ranged gameplay
- Many possible moves are better than going face-to-face
- Enemies do not respect you in combat at all; instead, they're going for you at the same time
- Enemies do not have enough 'feedback' to the player when they're going to strike. Could work a bit more on SFX, VFX, or improve their animation
- Optimization needs more works
- Exploration, especially "parkour," is one of the most annoying in the game for mouse & keyboard users
- Recipe unlock can be really RNG and frustrating
- Gravity does its best to kill you every time
- Can't pet foxes

PS. Don't forget that it's an early access review. Once the game is fully released and I beat the game. I'll make sure to rewrite it!
